leads.summary: Trailing comma followed by a whole-line // comment now empties an otherwise valid menu file
leads.consequence: A user extension containing an entry ending in a comma, then a standalone comment, then `}` or `]`, parsed on quattro, now returns [] and drops all custom rows after upgrade or hot reload. The same pattern in the shipped default would empty default rows. The scanner looks past whitespace but not comments before deciding whether to keep a comma. Preserve the comma only if another item follows after skipping any allowed comments, or strip comments first with a string-aware pass.

leads.summary: Parser documentation still says inline // comments are rejected
leads.consequence: The documentation explicitly tells extension authors that only whole-line `//` is removed and an inline tail breaks parsing, while the new scanner accepts inline tails. Users will avoid the feature this patch exists to provide, and the docs' stated grammar no longer matches the implementation. Update the paragraph to describe inline `//` outside strings and clarify that `/* */` remains unsupported if this project intentionally supports only a subset of JSONC. Related #6525 and #13681 independently edit this paragraph, so coordinate the final wording.
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; Corroborates F2; published inside Suggested change

leads.summary: Inline comment scanner does not terminate at a bare carriage-return line ending
leads.consequence: In a user JSONC file written with bare CR line endings, `//` swallows everything through EOF and parseMenuJsonc returns [], losing user rows. This limitation also existed in the earlier whole-line-only implementation, so it is not a regression for existing configs, but the newly promised inline handling still misses this JSONC line shape; CRLF and LF work. Include `` as a line end (preserving a separating whitespace) if bare-CR JSONC is in scope.
leads.triage: dropped; Pre-existing on quattro (regex also only ends on \n), CR-only files negligible; not material

leads.summary: The new test misses a plausible comment-and-trailing-comma regression it currently ships
leads.consequence: The existing fixture tests full-line comments and a trailing comma separately, and new assertions test inline tails but none places a whole-line comment between a trailing comma and its closer. The current scanner passes all new assertions while failing the previously valid combined shape in C1, so add that assertion to the test file, with an object and optionally an aliases array, to guard the fix. This is subordinate to C1, not an additional runtime defect.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** A trailing comma followed by a whole-line `//` comment before `}` or `]` now empties the menu file (it parsed on `quattro`).

### Comma lookahead does not skip comments

The comma check in `stripJsonc` (`MenuModel.js:24-28`) skips only whitespace: a comma before a comment is kept, the comment is stripped, and `JSON.parse` sees `, }`. `quattro` removed whole-line comments before the comma pass. **Impact:** a commented-out last entry after a trailing comma makes `parseMenuJsonc` return `[]`, dropping every user row; uncommenting the three `"personal"` examples in the shipped sample extension gives 3 rows on `quattro` and 0 here. It also still breaks `"a": {...}, // note` as the last entry.

**Suggested change:** let the comma lookahead skip `//` comments as well as whitespace, add assertions for both layouts, and update `docs/menu.md:15-19`, which still says only whole-line comments are removed.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at f75205f)</summary>

# Reproducer: trailing comma followed by a `//` comment before the closer

Finding: the new single-pass `stripJsonc` keeps a trailing comma whenever the next non-whitespace character is `/`, then strips the comment, so `JSON.parse` sees `, }` and the whole file parses to `[]`. Whole-line comments in that position worked before this PR (they were removed before the comma pass), so this is a regression; inline comments in that position were already broken and stay broken.

## Test (menu-test.sh style)

Save as `test/shell.d/jsonc-comment-before-closer-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/jsonc-comment-before-closer-test.sh` from the repository root. Each check is in its own file because a failed assertion ends the file.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

run_node_test <<'JS'
const menu = requireFromRoot('shell/plugins/menu/MenuModel.js')

// A commented-out last entry is a whole-line comment between a trailing comma
// and the closing brace.
assertEqual(
  menu.parseMenuJsonc('{\n  "a": {"label": "A"},\n  // "b": {"label": "B"},\n}').length,
  1,
  'menu drops a trailing comma when a whole-line comment sits between it and the closer'
)
JS
```

Actual output at PR head `f75205f9`:

```text
expected: 1
actual:   0
not ok - menu drops a trailing comma when a whole-line comment sits between it and the closer
```

Actual output at `quattro` tip `e332dc97` and at #13255 head `5771ffe9`:

```text
ok - menu drops a trailing comma when a whole-line comment sits between it and the closer
```

The same file with this PR merged into `quattro` fails the same way as the PR head.

## Realistic trigger: the shipped sample extension

`config/omarchy/extensions/omarchy-menu.jsonc` ships as `{`, a block of `//` comments with commented-out example rows, and `}`. Uncommenting the three `"personal"` example rows leaves each with its trailing comma and more comment lines below them before `}`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

run_node_test <<'JS'
const fs = require('fs')
const menu = requireFromRoot('shell/plugins/menu/MenuModel.js')
const sample = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'config/omarchy/extensions/omarchy-menu.jsonc'), 'utf8')

// Uncomment the three "personal" example rows the shipped sample extension offers.
const edited = sample.replace(/^  \/\/ ("personal[^"]*": \{[^\n]*)$/gm, '  $1')
assertEqual(
  menu.parseMenuJsonc(edited).map(item => item.id).join(','),
  'personal,personal.notes,personal.files',
  'menu loads the example rows uncommented in the sample extension'
)
JS
```

Actual output at PR head `f75205f9`:

```text
expected: personal,personal.notes,personal.files
actual:   
not ok - menu loads the example rows uncommented in the sample extension
```

Actual output at `quattro` tip `e332dc97` and at #13255 head `5771ffe9`:

```text
ok - menu loads the example rows uncommented in the sample extension
```

## Inline comment after the last trailing comma (same cause, not a regression)

```js
assertEqual(
  menu.parseMenuJsonc('{\n  "a": {"label": "A"}, // note\n}').length,
  1,
  'menu drops a trailing comma when an inline comment follows it on the last entry'
)
```

Actual output at PR head `f75205f9` (also at `quattro` and #13255, which never stripped inline comments):

```text
expected: 1
actual:   0
not ok - menu drops a trailing comma when an inline comment follows it on the last entry
```

## Stripped text at PR head

```text
input:  {\n  "a": {"label": "A"},\n  // "b": {"label": "B"},\n}
output: {\n  "a": {"label": "A"},\n  }        <- JSON.parse rejects the comma

input:  {\n  "a": {"label": "A"}, // note\n}
output: {\n  "a": {"label": "A"}, }
```

## Checked fix

Letting the comma lookahead skip `//` comments as well as whitespace makes all three checks above pass, and `menu-test.sh` and `menu-guards-test.sh` still pass (the tested copy differed from this only by a two-line code comment):

```diff
     } else if (ch === ",") {
       var next = i + 1
-      while (next < input.length && /\s/.test(input[next])) next++
+      while (next < input.length) {
+        if (/\s/.test(input[next])) {
+          next++
+        } else if (input[next] === "/" && input[next + 1] === "/") {
+          while (next < input.length && input[next] !== "\n") next++
+        } else {
+          break
+        }
+      }
       if (next >= input.length || (input[next] !== "}" && input[next] !== "]"))
         out += ch
```
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** at `f75205f` in Node:
- An inline tail after the closing brace (#13493) and an inline comment between entries now parse (0 items on `quattro`, 1 and 2 here).
- Commas before `]` or `}` inside strings stay intact (#13250), as do `//` inside strings, escaped quotes and CRLF files.
- The shipped `default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc` parses to identical items with this parser and with `quattro`'s, both for the PR's copy (340 items) and for `quattro`'s (344).
- `menu-test.sh` and `menu-guards-test.sh` pass at the head and with the PR merged into `quattro`; the new regression assertions fail on `quattro` (the `A // B` guard passes on both).

**Related PRs:** #13681 uses the same whitespace-only comma lookahead. #13305 and #6525 change the same `stripJsonc` lines. This branch contains both commits of #13255, so if it lands first, #13255 is superseded.
</details>
